title: EEOC Technical Assistance — AI and Title VII adverse impact in employment selection
description: Non-binding EEOC technical assistance explaining how existing Title VII disparate-impact principles apply to algorithmic/AI employment-selection tools. Not a statutory or regulatory provision itself.
framework_name: EEOC Technical Assistance on AI and Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964
control_reference: Select Issues: Assessing Adverse Impact in Software, Algorithms, and Artificial Intelligence Used in Employment Selection Procedures
control_text: Existing Title VII disparate-impact principles apply to employers' use of algorithmic decision-making tools and AI in employment selection procedures (hiring, promotion, firing); employers may remain liable for adverse impact caused by such tools even when built or administered by a third-party vendor, and passing a bright-line statistical threshold (e.g. the 'four-fifths rule') does not by itself guarantee a tool will not be found to have an unlawful disparate impact.

citations.title: Select Issues: Assessing Adverse Impact in Software, Algorithms, and Artificial Intelligence Used in Employment Selection Procedures Under Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964

relationships.reason: Satisfying this guidance's expectations requires a documented bias audit demonstrating adverse impact was assessed.
